hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built
hard_gates.evidence: My own attacks found no leak. As alnoor's admin I made 24 API calls against gulfsteel's admin, a second B user, the B Administrator role and the B Read-only role. They covered GET, PUT (including an e-mail move), password, unblock, revoke, DELETE, role PUT/DELETE/copy, create-with-B-role, search and filter by B values, a tenant query parameter and tenant headers. Every call by id answered 404, searches returned nothing of B's, B's records read back unchanged, and B's admin still signed in. I also hit B's private and shared saved views 12 ways: all 404 (attacks/attack-a-vs-b.txt). As erp_app: 0 rows with no tenant bound. Bound to A, 0 of B's rows and UPDATE 0. An insert into B was refused by RLS. A session-level or forged app.tenant_tx tenant was ignored. Credentials and sign_in_secret were denied, SET ROLE was refused, and RLS could not be disabled (attacks/db-app-role.txt). No export, job or file endpoints exist yet.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches a tenant leak planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L7 (plants/L7-role-name-registry.diff) keeps a role-name registry outside the tenant's rows, so POST /api/identity/roles and /roles/{id}/copy answer 409 identity.roleNameTaken for a name another workspace uses. With it in place all 93 gate tests pass (plants/plant-L7-gates.log) and so do all 74 identity tests (plant-L7-identity-tests.log). Proof (plants/CriticRoleNameOracleProof.cs, plant-L7-proof.log): tenant B creates 'JAFZA payroll …', then tenant A gets 409 for that name and 201 for an unused one. Without the plant both answer 201 (proofs-unplanted-control.log). G1WriteOracle judges only e-mail and code fields, so name fields are never checked for write oracles.

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions of the product (restricted roles, escalation)
hard_gates.evidence: No escalation was found in the shipped product. The Read-only user gets no New user or New role, the user panel shows only Details, What they can do and Close, the role matrix has 0 enabled checkboxes, and POST /api/identity/roles from that browser answers 403 (browser-walk.txt, screenshot 04). Unplanted, a helpdesk clerk gets 403 on all five partial-grant attacks (proofs-unplanted-control.log). Round 2's P5 is now caught: 3 G2 failures (plants/r2-P5-recheck-G2.log).

hard_gates.gate: G2 gate catches permission faults planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plants P14 and P16 (plants/P14-P16.diff) make the access checks look only at identity.* permissions: UserAccess.WithinCallerAsync, and the role create, update, delete and copy grant checks. All 303 .NET tests pass: gates 93, identity 74, kernel 127, lists 6, tenancy 3 (plants/plant-P14-P16-all-dotnet.log). No e2e spec uses a non-identity permission. Proof (plants/CriticPartialGrantProof.cs, plant-P14-P16-proof.log): a clerk holding only identity permissions acts on a 'Workspace manager' (tenancy.tenant.read and update). The clerk resets the manager's password (200), moves their sign-in (200), creates a role granting tenancy.tenant.update (201), and renames and empties the manager role (200). UI plant U2, the same narrowing in the screen's beyondOwn check, passes all 146 web unit tests (plants/plant-U2-web-unit.log).

odoo.notes: Median of 3 runs each, blind, with the shipped drivers (compare/comparisons/create-restricted-user.json). Human plus wait was 19.96 s against 34.73 s. Ours: Users > Alt+N > e-mail (the name is filled from it) > the role > Ctrl+Enter. Caveat unchanged since r1: there is no contacts permission, so 'view and create contacts only' cannot be built, and the 'Clerk (restricted)' role (own profile only) was used.

Shortest expert path in each, median of 3 (compare-find-user-short/). Ours typed the word prefixes 'maj an pi' (9 rows) and clicked the user. Odoo used Ctrl+K /users and typed the contiguous fragment 'd anil p' + Enter (7 rows). Keystrokes tie 9-9 and human seconds lose, 9.97 against 9.84: a loss. biggest_gap.title: The takeover and grant gates only aim at a record that grants everything, so a wrongly narrowed check that lets a clerk take over a non-identity manager goes unseen
biggest_gap.detail:
G2AccountTakeoverTests, GrantBearingRecords and the screens-hide matrix always use the strongest record as the target: the Administrator, or a role holding the whole catalogue. Every caller they build holds only identity permissions. A check that compares only part of the target's grants therefore still answers 403 against the Administrator, and every gate passes. Plants P14 and P16 make UserAccess and the role grant checks compare identity.* permissions only.

Result: a helpdesk clerk with users.update and resetPassword takes over the 'Workspace manager' (tenancy permissions). The clerk sets the manager's password, moves their sign-in, mints a role granting tenancy.tenant.update, and empties the manager's role. All 303 .NET tests and all 146 web tests stay green.

Once Contacts, Purchasing and Accounting land, most strong accounts in a UAE trading company will hold non-identity permissions: the finance manager, the purchasing approver. This class of fault is exactly the one that lets a junior administrator take them over.

Fix:
- Aim every acting-on-a-user and acting-on-a-role probe at targets whose grants are disjoint from the caller's and only partly overlap them. Include one grant from every module in the catalogue, not only the Administrator, and include a test module the way ModulePermissionsTests does.
- Add P14/P16 as gate self-tests.
- Add a non-identity permission to the screens test catalogue and its stronger-user case (U2).
- Separately, extend G1WriteOracle to name fields (L7): a role created by B, then A's same-name create, must answer like an unused name.
biggest_gap.evidence:
In a clone of c02d93a:
1. git apply gauntlet/evidence/p03-identity/r3/plants/P14-P16.diff
2. dotnet test Erp.slnx -c Release gives Gates 93/93, Identity 74/74, Kernel 127/127, Lists 6/6, Tenancy 3/3 (plants/plant-P14-P16-all-dotnet.log).
3. Copy plants/CriticPartialGrantProof.cs to tests/Erp.Modules.Identity.Tests/ and run with --filter CriticPartialGrantProof. The answers are: reset password 200, move sign-in 200, grant the helper the manager role 403, create a role with tenancy.tenant.update 201, rename and empty the manager role 200 (plants/plant-P14-P16-proof.log). Without the plant all five answer 403 (plants/proofs-unplanted-control.log).
4. UI: git apply plants/U2-ui-beyond-own-identity-only.diff, then in web run npx vitest run: 146/146 (plants/plant-U2-web-unit.log).
5. Leak: python3 plants/apply-L7.py, then dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests gives 93/93 (plants/plant-L7-gates.log). CriticRoleNameOracleProof.cs shows 409 for B's role name and 201 for an unused one (plants/plant-L7-proof.log).

other_findings: [route: p00-foundation] G1WriteOracle treats only e-mail and code fields as identifying (IsIdentifying), and the HTTP attack and non-interference phases judge differential answers on GETs only. A cross-tenant uniqueness registry on any name field (role names, later item names, contact names) passes every gate. L7 is the concrete case on this piece's surface (plants/plant-L7-gates.log). Fix it in the shared write oracle so every module's create and rename endpoints are covered.

Scope gap unchanged since r1: there is no per-user default company and no role assignment per company. The user form has no company field (browser-walk.txt), identity.user_roles has no company column, and no company concept exists at this commit. The piece spec requires both. 'Accountant in the Dubai LLC, read-only in the JAFZA entity' still cannot be expressed.

Arabic search gap: the users list searches displayName and email only (searchFields in /api/lists/identity.users/definition). An Arabic administrator sees Arabic names in the list, but searching 'ماجد' or 'ماجد بيلاي' returns 0 of 100,004 users, through the API too (browser-walk.txt). Finding a colleague by the name as written in Arabic does not work.

find-user ranking: 'maj ani pil' lists 'Rania Majid Pillai' above 'Majid Anil Pillai'. Ranking does not prefer the query's word order, so the target is the second row. The shipped ours find-user driver also clicks the already-focused search box, an extra step that costs the full-name comparison on human seconds (14.35 against 13.2; compare/comparisons/find-user.json).

[route: p05-list-search] At 1440 px the users grid's cells still drift off their headers for longer e-mails: the Language, Status and Last sign-in columns shift right, and Roles is cut (screenshots 01 and 04). This was also reported in r2.

Lockout behind Docker: every failed attempt is recorded from 172.19.0.1, the compose gateway (screenshot 07). After 7 failures the right password was refused from that client, and 'Allow sign-in again' restored it (200). compose.yaml sets no Erp__Http__KnownProxies, so a default deployment lets one attacker pause an account for every user behind the same proxy (unchanged since r1).
create-restricted-user still uses 'Clerk (restricted)' because no contacts permission exists. The win does not yet show the bar's 'view and create contacts only' role.

Positive and fixed since r2:
- r2 P5 (e-mail-only edit skipping the access check) is caught by three G2 tests.
- The Read-only user sees no New user or New role.
- Alt+N opens new user and new role from the focused search box.
- The sign-in history no longer clips: rows are stacked in the panel in English, and the Arabic table is 314 px wide in a 338 px panel.
- Space and Ctrl+Enter deactivate a user and end their live session.
- A user created with language ar opens right to left.
- The role matrix has search, 'Select all shown' and per-column bulk toggles, and works by keyboard.
- The Arabic role panel contains no Latin words.
- No console errors or 5xx responses during the walk.
- Test counts rose from 534 to 643.

Harness notes:
- Gate runs took 14 to 17 minutes at load average about 17 from other agents.
- verify's Testcontainers still bind random host ports outside the critic's port block, and this cannot be overridden.
- Odoo machine seconds were 2.1 to 2.4 s for find-user and 6.5 to 7.0 s for create-restricted-user. Ours wins machine seconds on both tasks.
